item.title: Most of G-7 Is Spending More on Interest Than Defense, Scope Says
item.description: Every Group of Seven country apart from Germany and Canada now faces interest costs that exceed defense expenditure, Scope Ratings said.

item.title: Bank of Korea Minutes Back More Hikes on Inflation, Growth
item.description: The Bank of Korea saw a need for further interest-rate hikes after last month’s increase, as stronger growth threatened to keep inflation elevated and financial stability risks continued to build, minutes from July’s meeting showed.

item.title: Risk Demand Grows for Europe as AI Woes Hit US, Citi’s Chew Says
item.description: Europe’s stock market is the only major region to have experienced a meaningful improvement in risk appetite in recent weeks, supported by fresh capital inflows and better-than-expected earnings, according to strategists at Citigroup Inc.

item.title: KKR-Backed Infinx Services Said to Weigh $300 Million India IPO
item.description: Infinx Services Pvt., a healthcare revenue cycle management company, is considering an initial public offering of as much as $300 million in India, according to people familiar with the matter, joining a growing pipeline of healthcare services firms seeking to tap the country’s buoyant equity markets.

item.title: Bond Funds Turn to Europe as Global Risks Become Harder to Price
item.description: European bonds are emerging as a safer choice for fund managers as they try to navigate an increasingly fraught global backdrop.

item.title: Apple’s India Sales Top $10 Billion on Widening Retail Push
item.description: Apple Inc. exceeded $10 billion in annual sales in India for the first time last fiscal year, underscoring surging demand for its pricey devices in a market where it’s steadily ramping up its retail network.

item.title: Aramco Says July Attacks Had No Material Operational Impact
item.description: Saudi Aramco said attacks last month didn’t have a material impact on its operations, and the company is working to expand its oil export capacity as the Iran war disrupts flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: HSBC to Consider Hiking Bonus Pool If Performance Keeps Up
item.description: HSBC Holdings Plc Chief Executive Officer Georges Elhedery said the lender will consider boosting its bonus pool for bankers if strong performance continues.

item.title: US Defense Agency Cancels Plan to Buy $300 Million of Lithium
item.description: The US Department of Defense has canceled a tender to purchase lithium for its strategic stockpiles, in another apparent sign of the challenges it faces in trying to bolster supplies of critical minerals.

item.title: Huawei’s Top Scientist Warns of Chip Limit Nvidia Will Soon Face
item.description: Huawei Technologies Co.’s top semiconductor scientist warned of the looming physical limits Western chipmaking giants including Nvidia Corp. face in their pursuit of more powerful processors, in a rare public appearance streamed in China.

item.title: Copper Marches Closer to $14,000 as Flows to US Tighten Market
item.description: Copper advanced to the highest in two months, nearing $14,000 a ton in London, as traders monitored ballooning volumes held in the US ahead of an expected decision on an import tariff by President Donald Trump.

item.title: Chinese Startup AI² Robotics Is Said to Consider Hong Kong IPO
item.description: Chinese robot maker AI² Robotics is considering an initial public offering in Hong Kong, according to people familiar with the matter, looking to tap into interest for the growing sector.

item.title: Europe’s Earnings Are Much Stronger Than They Look
item.description: Europe Inc. is delivering one of the strongest earnings scorecards in years, setting up regional stocks to scale fresh peaks as analysts turn even more optimistic about a broad range of sectors.

item.title: FTSE 100 Live: UK Stock Futures Rise, Pound Eases on Busy Earnings Day
item.description: FTSE 100 Live: UK Stock Futures Rise, Pound Eases on Busy Earnings Day【原文：FTSE 100 Live: UK Stock Futures Rise, Pound Eases on Busy Earnings Day】

item.title: Bayer Earnings Beat Estimates on Crop Science Strength
item.description: Bayer AG posted better-than-expected profit in the second quarter, helped by a strong performance in its crop science business.

item.title: BlackRock Launches Tokenized Money Market Funds in Europe
item.description: BlackRock Inc. is bringing blockchain technology to its flagship money market funds in Europe, in the latest sign of Wall Street’s growing ambition to expand use of digital-asset technology in mainstream finance.

item.title: Lufthansa Warns of Profit Risk as Jet Fuel Surge Roils Industry
item.description: Deutsche Lufthansa AG warned of heightened uncertainty for its full-year outlook as volatility in jet fuel prices and shortened booking cycles complicate efforts to boost profit.

item.title: Chinese Dip-Buying Bolsters Gold as Prices Find Floor at $4,000
item.description: Chinese institutional investors have swooped on gold in recent weeks, helping to arrest the precious metal’s decline and keep prices above the key threshold of $4,000 an ounce.

item.title: China’s AI Blitz Creates ‘Death Zone’ for Rival US Model Makers
item.description: A flurry of model launches from China’s AI sector is rapidly narrowing the gap with Silicon Valley and creating what’s been described as a death zone for anyone without frontier-pushing technology or market-breaking pricing.

item.title: Big AI Bets Divide Venture Capital, Leaving Smaller Funds Behind
item.description: Early last year, venture capital firm Felix Capital set out to raise $600 million for its next fund, touting previous investments in fitness-machine maker Peloton Interactive Inc. and food-delivery service Deliveroo. But investors want to see returns from older funds before they commit new capital, and Felix is still $150 million short of its target, according to a person with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: Citi Says Japan Has Yen Defense Tools Beyond Treasury Sales
item.description: Japan has alternative tools to defend the yen without liquidating its more than $1.1 trillion US Treasury portfolio as its short-term debt holdings run low, according to Citigroup Inc.

item.title: Katayama Says US Evaluates Japan’s Economic Policies Highly
item.description: Washington evaluates Japan’s economic policies highly, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said, sidestepping a question on whether the US helped Japan strengthen the yen out of concern over Tokyo’s financial markets.

item.title: Modi Seeks Sweeping Tax Cuts for Electronics Firms, Global Funds
item.description: India will seek parliamentary approval for tax changes to spur foreign investment and local manufacturing, according to people with knowledge of the matter, as Prime Minister Narendra Modi works to refocus the administration on his economic agenda after recent student protests.

item.title: Apple Briefly Removes Telegram App For Child Abuse Content
item.description: Apple Inc. briefly removed the Telegram messaging app from its App Store after finding content on the platform that violated a ban on child sexual abuse material.

item.title: Confusion Over India NSE Closing Auction Turbocharges Nifty Rally
item.description: The new rules were meant to improve price discovery and curb manipulation in the final stretch of trading.

item.title: South Korea’s Leveraged ETF Trading Plummets Under New Curbs
item.description: Trading in leveraged exchange-traded funds tied to South Korea’s two chip giants has shrunk sharply, after authorities took steps to slow demand for the products that fueled recent market volatility.

item.title: Iron Ore Dips to 13-Month Low in Threat to Higher-Cost Supply
item.description: Iron ore traded near a 13-month low, pushing the market to levels that may threaten some higher-cost production.

item.title: After Historic Intervention, 155 Emerges as Yen’s Next Big Test
item.description: Japan’s historic joint intervention with the US is shifting market focus to whether the yen can strengthen beyond 155 per dollar, a threshold strategists view as the key test for the rally’s staying power.

item.title: Alibaba-Backed 3D-Modeling Startup Vast Is Said to Weigh HK IPO
item.description: Vast, a 3D-modeling startup, is considering an initial public offering in Hong Kong, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: Australia Household Spending Jumps as Fuel Spike Drives EV Surge
item.description: Australia’s household spending surged beyond estimates in June as consumers accelerated a shift to electric vehicles in response to persistently elevated fuel prices.
